newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Beach to drill five wells in U.S..
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Beach to drill five wells in U.S..

text.p: Beach Petroleum NL said on Wednesday it will next week begin a five well drilling programme at its South Burbank Unit (SBU) in the United States to boost the company's producing onshore oil reserves.

The company said in a statment it was targeting deeper formations at Burbank in Oklahoma, which contributed 53,000 barrels of oil to Beach's production totals last year through its 76.2 percent interest in the field.

Beach chief executive Reg Nelson said the bulk of existing oil production in the field was from the relatively shallow Burbank sandstone formation and there had been no substantial investigation of its deeper potential reservoir formations.
The new drilling programme would deepen existing wells in SBU to test the Mississippi Chat, a proven producer elsewhere in the region, he said.

"The Mississippi Chat formation beneath the Burbank sandstone exists at depths of approximately 870 metres but its distribution throughout the field is not well understood as few wells have penetrated this reservoir," he said.
The drilling programme should be completed by the end of January 1997, he said.
Nelson last month told Reuters Beach was planning seismic surveys beneath the shallow Burbank sands before considering further options for the holding which could include divestment.
